scope: Source-checked research for v 0.84.60 sarcoma patient content; not independent clinical approval. Product risk summaries do not establish regimen-specific incidence or replace NCCP/local prescribing guidance.

agents.source_title: HPRA Doxorubicin 2 mg/ml SmPC, 1 February 2023; current product-page link checked
agents.mechanism: An anthracycline that binds DNA and disrupts processes needed for cell replication.
common_or_expected: Marrow suppression, nausea/vomiting, hair loss, mouth inflammation, appetite loss and diarrhoea.
serious_or_lasting: Cumulative heart-muscle damage and heart failure can emerge after treatment; rhythm disturbances also occur.
Severe infection or bleeding from low counts; rare secondary acute leukaemia, especially with other DNA-damaging treatment.
Leakage outside the vein can cause tissue destruction requiring surgery.
agents.monitoring: Check prior anthracycline exposure, cardiac history/function, blood counts and liver function. Apply the NCCP protocol and local cardiac-monitoring policy rather than transplanting this product's frequency into the regimen.
agents.patient_action: Tell staff immediately about infusion-site pain/burning. Obtain urgent advice for fever/unwellness, breathing or chest symptoms. Temporary red urine can reflect drug colour; painful urination, clots or persisting red urine need assessment.
agents.source_caveat: The authorised example product is listed as not marketed; confirm the actual supplied formulation's SmPC. Do not present the SmPC's pooled cardiac percentage as this sarcoma regimen's personal risk.

agents.source_title: HPRA Mitoxana 1 g SmPC, 11 September 2023; current product-page link checked
agents.mechanism: Liver activation produces an alkylating medicine that cross-links DNA and interrupts cell division.
common_or_expected: Low counts, infection risk, nausea/vomiting, hair loss and mucosal effects.
serious_or_lasting: Encephalopathy may cause confusion, marked drowsiness, hallucinations or seizures; recovery is usual but not guaranteed.
Bladder bleeding and kidney/tubular injury, electrolyte loss, renal failure and possible delayed progression after treatment.
Fertility damage/premature menopause and secondary malignancies; serious cardiac or pulmonary toxicity.
agents.monitoring: Blood counts, renal/tubular function, electrolytes, urine for blood and mental state before/during/after treatment. Mesna and prescribed hydration reduce bladder toxicity; they do not establish protection against all kidney or brain injury.
agents.patient_action: Report altered thinking or unusual sleepiness immediately, and urgently report bloody/painful urine, reduced urine, fever or breathing changes. Keep the complete prescribed mesna schedule even after the chemotherapy infusion ends.
agents.source_caveat: Use exact NCCP adult mesna/hydration timing, not the product's paediatric example schedules.

agents.source_title: HPRA Gemcitabine 200 mg powder SmPC, 4 June 2024
agents.mechanism: Active metabolites reduce DNA building blocks and enter growing DNA strands, interrupting further DNA synthesis.
common_or_expected: Low counts, nausea, flu-like symptoms, rash, swelling, fatigue and liver-test changes.
serious_or_lasting: Pneumonitis or other serious lung injury.
Haemolytic uraemic syndrome: blood-cell damage with kidney failure that can persist and require dialysis.
Capillary leak with swelling, low blood pressure or breathing difficulty; PRES with headache, confusion, seizures or visual loss; severe blistering/peeling skin reactions.
Potential fertility harm; discuss preservation before treatment.
agents.monitoring: Counts before each dose, periodic renal/liver tests and review of lung, skin, neurological and fluid symptoms.
agents.patient_action: Urgently report new breathlessness, reduced urine, unusual bruising, sudden widespread swelling/faintness, severe headache/confusion/visual change, or blistering skin. Fever cannot safely be assumed to be a harmless flu-like effect.
agents.source_caveat: Product warnings about prolonged infusion do not override NCCP 00501: its 675 mg/m² dose is deliberately infused over 90 minutes. Do not substitute a 30-minute schedule or another gemcitabine dose.

agents.source_title: EMA Taxotere product information; EPAR lists update 22 October 2026
agents.mechanism: Stabilises microtubules, preventing normal rearrangement of the machinery that separates chromosomes during cell division.
common_or_expected: Low counts, infection, hair loss, mouth/bowel effects, fatigue, nail changes, neuropathy and fluid retention.
serious_or_lasting: Severe infusion allergy, enterocolitis/perforation, pneumonitis and severe skin reactions.
Peripheral nerve symptoms may persist; permanent hair loss has been reported.
Visual disturbance may reflect macular swelling; serious liver injury is possible.
agents.monitoring: Blood counts and liver tests; assess neuropathy, skin/nails, fluid retention, breathing and vision. Prescribed dexamethasone reduces hypersensitivity severity and fluid retention.
agents.patient_action: Immediately report infusion tightness, wheeze or faintness. Urgently report fever, severe abdominal pain/diarrhoea, breathlessness, blistering rash or visual change. Report numbness before another dose.
agents.source_caveat: Use NCCP 00501's day-7-start steroid schedule. Do not import prostate premedication, other combinations' G-CSF mandates, efficacy or incidence. Check actual formulation excipients.

agents.mechanism: Liver metabolism activates the medicine; metabolites damage DNA and inhibit DNA synthesis and cell growth.
common_or_expected: Nausea/vomiting, appetite loss and marrow suppression. Count nadirs can be delayed until 3–4 weeks.
Flu-like illness, skin/sun sensitivity and hair changes can occur.
serious_or_lasting: Severe infection/bleeding; rare allergic reactions or kidney impairment.
Rare hepatic veno-occlusive disease can rapidly progress to liver necrosis and death.
Leakage outside the vein can cause tissue injury. Discuss fertility preservation because the medicine can damage genetic material.
agents.monitoring: Blood counts, liver and renal function during/after therapy, with attention to delayed marrow toxicity and symptoms of liver injury.
agents.patient_action: Urgently report fever/unwellness, bleeding, persistent vomiting, severe abdominal pain or jaundice; immediately report infusion-site burning. Flu-like symptoms must not delay assessment for infection.
agents.source_caveat: Do not import another indication's dose or quote a 1 g/m² trial as direct evidence for NCCP 00511's 1.2 g/m² schedule.

trials.summary: Randomised phase III, 257 previously untreated advanced/unresectable/metastatic STS patients. Doxorubicin 75 mg/m² day 1 versus gemcitabine 675 mg/m² days 1/8 over 90 minutes plus docetaxel 75 mg/m² day 8 over 60 minutes; 21-day cycles, up to six. Alive/progression-free at 24 weeks:46.3% versus 46.4%. Median PFS 23.3 versus 23.7 weeks; no superiority shown for gemcitabine/docetaxel. Trial G-CSF was permitted after febrile neutropenia according to local policy.
trials.applicability: The drug dose/timing matches NCCP 00501. Supports a first-line comparison, not an individual survival forecast, later-line efficacy estimate or proof of superiority in leiomyosarcoma. Current treatment selection remains histology/context-specific. Use current NCCP supportive care, not archived trial instructions.

trials.summary: Randomised phase III, 455 patients aged 18–60 with advanced high-grade STS and WHO PS 0–1. Doxorubicin 75 mg/m² versus doxorubicin 75 mg/m² plus ifosfamide 10 g/m² over 4 days with mesna/pegfilgrastim. Combination versus monotherapy: response 26% versus 14%; median PFS 7.4 versus 4.6 months; median OS 14.3 versus 12.8 months, no statistically significant OS difference (HR 0.83, 95.5%CI 0.67–1.03, p=0.076). Grade 3/4 febrile neutropenia 46% versus 13%.
trials.applicability: Contextual rationale for greater tumour shrinkage at increased toxicity. Neither NCCP 00391 (dox 60/ifo 9 g) nor 00392 (dox 75/ifo 9 g) is identical. Do not label these numbers regimen-specific or claim curative/neoadjuvant benefit from this advanced-disease trial.

trials.summary: Historical single-arm phaseII after previous chemotherapy:50 enrolled, 44 response-evaluable. Dacarbazine 1.2 g/m² over 20 minutes every 3 weeks. One complete and seven partial responses:18% of evaluable patients (95%CI 7–29). Haematological toxicity was dose-limiting.
trials.applicability: Direct dose/schedule evidence for the 1.2 g/m² approach, but small, old, uncontrolled and not evidence of survival benefit. The denominator is 44 evaluable, not all 50 enrolled. Do not convert 18% into a personal probability.

trials.summary: Eribulin phaseIII used investigator-selected dacarbazine 850, 1000 or 1200 mg/m²; its pooled comparator results are not specific to 1200. Trabectedin phaseIII used dacarbazine 1000 mg/m², not 1200. Both enrolled selected previously treated liposarcoma/leiomyosarcoma populations; do not generalise their results to every sarcoma subtype or line.

existing_agent_content_spot_check: 00500, 00391, 00392, 00501 and 00511 profiles were absent at inspection; this is an omission check against reusable agent entries, not a complete audit of all existing profiles.
00260 doxorubicin already covers delayed heart damage, extravasation and rare later blood cancers; keep these visible in the new consent.
00602 ifosfamide already correctly separates mesna bladder protection from renal/brain injury; retain this distinction and include lasting renal/fertility risk.

00281 gemcitabine reusable entry says rare lung/kidney injury but does not explicitly name SCAR, PRES, capillary leak or potentially irreversible HUS renal injury. Include these in detailed risk/urgent-action content.
00204 docetaxel reusable entry omits severe gut/lung/skin toxicity, permanent alopecia and urgent visual symptoms. Include these without implying that they are common.
00464 dacarbazine already covers severe liver injury and infusion injury; make delayed 3–4-week marrow suppression and jaundice/abdominal-pain escalation explicit in sarcoma content.
